title: The Questions You Keep Avoiding May Decide the Future of Your Marriage
paragraphs:
The Questions You Keep Avoiding May Decide the Future of Your Marriage
Hard Questions Every Christian Couple Should Answer Before Life Answers Them for You
Some relationships do not collapse because love disappeared.

Long before divorce papers are signed...
before another person's name appears in hidden messages...
before silent dinners become normal...
before prayers become routine...
before church attendance becomes performance...
Questions everybody hoped would somehow answer themselves.
One of the greatest tragedies inside Christian relationships is not the absence of love—it is the presence of assumptions.
But Scripture never teaches that spiritual maturity grows where truth is avoided.

"Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ."
(John 1:17)
Jesus never separated grace from truth.
Many relationships are built on chemistry.
Kingdom marriages are built on confession.
The Bible never portrays healthy relationships as people who never struggle.
It portrays redeemed people who continually bring darkness into God's light.
The Greek word for fellowship is:
John does not say fellowship comes from pretending.
It comes from walking in the light.
That is why every Christian couple should wrestle with questions that are uncomfortable before life forces the answers.
Can we truly forgive each other?
"Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Up to seven times?"
"I do not say to you, up to seven times, but up to seventy-seven times."
Forgiveness is not pretending nothing happened.
The Greek word Jesus uses repeatedly throughout the New Testament is:
It is not saying the wound never existed.
It is refusing to let the wound own the future.
Christian marriages cannot survive without forgiveness because two imperfect sinners cannot build a perfect relationship.
Who is really leading our home?
"Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ."
Many stop reading there or misuse what follows.
But the context begins with mutual submission under Christ.
means willingly arranging oneself under God's order.
It was never permission for abuse.
"The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve."
"Everyone should be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger."
The Greek phrase "quick to hear" implies eager attentiveness.
Many arguments are not won because one person had better logic.
They end because one person finally felt heard.
Do we pursue holiness more than happiness?
"How can I glorify My Father by loving sacrificially?"
Biblical marriage is two people helping each other become more like Christ.
What idols are quietly replacing God?
Even ministry can become an idol if Christ is no longer at the centre.
The Hebrew word for glory is:
Whatever carries the greatest weight in your life becomes what you worship.
If Christ is no longer the heaviest reality in your marriage...
"When I kept silent, my bones wasted away."
"Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed."
Would our children learn Jesus by watching us?
Not by listening to our worship playlist.
Not by reading our social media captions.
Children remember atmosphere more than speeches.
"As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."
The Hebrew word for serve is:
It means worship through devoted service.
Marriage is not merely living together.
One day every Christian marriage will stand before Christ.
That was secured by grace through faith in Jesus Christ alone.
But to give an account for stewardship.
How did we honour Him when nobody was watching?
This is why the Gospel changes everything.
The Bible is filled with scandal.
Yet every one of them became evidence that God delights in rewriting endings.
The greatest scandal in history was not humanity's sin.
It was that the spotless Son of God willingly carried it.
"The LORD has laid on Him the iniquity of us all."
Jesus did not merely improve broken people.
When both husband and wife continually kneel at the foot of the Cross, pride begins to die.
The greatest question every Christian couple must answer is not whether they love each other enough.
It is whether they love Christ enough to surrender everything else.
Because when Jesus truly becomes the centre...
even two people who thought their story was over discover that the Author never stopped writing.
One honest conversation started today could spare years of regret tomorrow.
The marriage surrendered to Christ will always outlast the marriage sustained only by emotion.
